title: Silent Titans - A look at the new artistic RPG Module from Patrick Stuart
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhXS2cpJlRo

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens what he intends as a year-long series on artistic RPG modules — the module as a work of art — and starts with a book that pushes the idea nearly to its limit. *Silent Titans*, written by Patrick Stuart and illustrated by Dirk Detweiler Leichty, arrived the day of filming, so this is a genuine first look rather than a review.

His central observation is a balance point: *Silent Titans* has taken the artistic module about as far as it can go while still being usable at a table. Any further toward pure art object and it stops functioning as a game master's tool. The evidence is in the flip-through — an isometric, almost graffiti-inflected visual style Daniel argues is badly underused in tabletop; a bookcloth hardcover under a dust jacket whose inner face is itself a map; rules for the ultralight Into the Odd system condensed onto a bookmark; and a setting (Wirral, the Sea of Broken Aeons, a dementia bomb inside a Titan's tower) written in prose he compares to Michael Cisco.

He's candid that he will probably never run it. Instead he reads modules like these as weird fiction, imagining the perfect session from both sides of the screen — a use case, he argues, that justifies the purchase on its own.

----

Do you buy RPG books you never intend to run — and if so, what are you actually getting out of them?
